title: Unit 6 — APA-06: Battery Discharge
description: Independently apply the MATLAB plotting workflow in the preloaded U06_APA06_BatteryPlots.m using its embedded battery data under an assumed constant 2.0 A load. Calculate power_A_W and power_B_W with element-wise voltage-times-current multiplication, retaining every sample. Build one figure with two vertically stacked panels: both voltage records and a horizontal 3.20 V cutoff drawn with ordinary plot above, and both calculated power records below. Distinguish the batteries by line style and/or marker shape and keep each battery's style consistent across panels. Give each panel a descriptive title, quantity/unit labels, a correctly associated legend, and grid. Use x limits [0,120] in both panels and choose y limits that include all values and the cutoff. Print each battery's final power from the calculated arrays, labeled with W units. Write 50–100 words as MATLAB comments identifying each battery's first supplied sample strictly below the cutoff, giving a numerical comparison and one limitation. Run File, inspect both panels, then Run Tests. Download the completed U06_APA06_BatteryPlots.m and separately export APA06_battery_comparison.png with the plot toolbar camera; submit both in Canvas.
note: The data are synthetic and 3.20 V is an exercise cutoff; no physical experiment is assigned. All starting data are in the script. Run Tests provides up to 10 code-check feedback points and never submits to Canvas or replaces its grade. Canvas rubric: Directions 30%; Compilation/syntax 15%; Runtime/input-output 30%; Correctness 25%. Canvas supplies points and due dates. Source calculation methods, interpretation, threshold reasoning, filenames, complete submission, and PNG readability/scale receive manual review. These discrete records do not establish exact crossing times, total energy capacity, behavior under other loads, or a universal battery ranking.
